output.reason: A few days of right-hand numbness and tingling that is worse at night, with the patient reporting no weakness, no face drooping and normal speech, fits a nerve-compression pattern manageable with self-care guidance plus a specific escalation plan, with no decision-critical clinician task established on the reported facts.
output.patientMessage: You can start self-care now: keep your wrist straight at night (a neutral wrist splint helps), and ease up on repetitive gripping, vibrating tools, or bent-wrist positions. Night-time hand tingling often comes from a pinched wrist nerve. If you develop hand weakness, dropping things, or constant numbness, message a Counsel clinician. If sudden face drooping, slurred speech, or arm weakness appears, call 911.
differential: Carpal tunnel syndrome (median nerve compression at the wrist)
